Hi Emily — appreciate the clear ask. Attached is a concise checklist + workbook (redwood_unit_econ_playbook_v1.xlsx) but here is the checklist in-line so procurement can circulate quickly: 

1) Instrumentation & telemetry (owner: HelixMed eng + Redwood SE)
   - Per-request metrics: tokens_in, tokens_out, model_variant, request_id, latency_ms (p50/p95/p99).
   - Aggregate metrics: tokens/day, tokens/unique_user, KV-cache hit rate, batch_size_distribution.

2) Traffic & request-size assumptions (baseline for pilot)
   - Typical prompt length: 60 tokens in, 120 tokens out (adjust based on your sample corpus).
   - Concurrency target: 50 concurrent streaming requests; burst to 150.
   - Batching policy: Redwood recommends continuous batching with max_batch_size=64 when latency SLO allows; expected effective per-request token cost reduction ~15–30% vs single-call.

3) Caching assumptions
   - Prefix/KV caching assumed for repeated prompts: conservative hit rate 20% for initial pilot, optimistic 35% when prompts are templated.
   - Cache behavior: KV cache reduces decode tokens only (saves tokens_out when repeated). Please confirm whether you expect heavy template reuse.

4) Pricing mapping & gates
   - Hosted price example used in workbook: $0.0025 per 1k input tokens / $0.013 per 1k output tokens (pilot price; dedicated pricing negotiated separately).
   - Acceptance gate for pilot: measured cost deviation from workbook projection <= 20% and p95 latency <= 800ms for 95% of calls.

5) Evaluation plan (owner: joint) — 14-day evaluation window
   - Day 0–2: instrument and sanity-run on 1000 sample requests.
   - Day 3–9: full traffic pilot; collect tokens/month projection, cache hit rate, batching effectiveness.
   - Day 10–14: run regression checks (response quality) and final cost reconciliation.

6) Deliverables for MAP sign-off
   - Instrumentation dashboard link + sample export (CSV)
   - Cost projection workbook (attached)
   - PO or procurement intent email

I've attached the workbook that maps your sample corpus to tokens/month and expected cost under the assumptions above (redwood_unit_econ_playbook_v1.xlsx). If you prefer, we can reduce the acceptance gate from 20% to 15% subject to an agreed measurement method.

Next steps: if this looks good I'll add these items to the MAP doc and loop in Marissa for commercial/discount thresholds.

Thanks Neha — this is great and very actionable. Two quick tweaks I suggest adding to the MAP so procurement has objective gates for commercial acceptance: 

- Evaluation acceptance thresholds (conservative):
  * Cost gate: realized cost per 1M tokens (input+output) must be within +15% of projected pilot workbook numbers. If >+15% we trigger an optimization window (3 business days) where Redwood will apply batching, cache tuning, or model variant fallback.
  * Quality gate: automated quality check (your eval set) shows <2% regression vs baseline on critical prompts.
  * Latency gate: p95 <= 600ms in-us region for 90% of samples; temporary spikes allowed for 5% of traffic.

- Measurement methodology: exports must include request-level token counts and model_variant; Redwood will provide a canonical CSV schema (see attached helix_cost-assumptions.csv).

- MAP milestones (mutual action plan)
  1) PO issued / procurement intent (target 2027-06-18)
  2) Pilot provisioning & instrumentation (Day 0–2)
  3) Pilot run (Day 3–16) 
  4) Evaluation & remediation (Day 17–19)
  5) Final decision: commit to Dedicated or extend pilot (Day 20)

If the cost gate fails after remediation we'll discuss either a temporary credit or rate adjustment while we iterate. Marissa / Ben — tagging you for any comments on acceptable remediation remedies or commercial concessions.
